plan: No capital at spot. Entry band $54-58 (brackets the 07-29 low of $53.87). Size 0.4% initial, 0.8% CAP - half the ruled cap, because the DEAL, not the business, sets the variance. Limits only. edge_explainer: TWO QUEUE PREMISES REFUTED. (1) Distribution date was 2025-10-30, not 10-20 (8-K 2025-10-30 Item 1.01; record 10-17, ratio 1:4, 158,727,456 shares) - all date-windowed stats keyed off 10-20 are wrong by seven sessions. (2) The week of 07-06 was NOT a guidance cut: on 2026-07-06 SOLS agreed to acquire Element Solutions for ~$14.5B ($10.00 cash + 0.500 SOLS per ESI share), ESI holders taking ~44% of the combined company, financed with a $4.685B committed Goldman bridge, pro-forma net leverage ~3.5x at close and explicitly sub-investment-grade. Guidance has been RAISED or reaffirmed at EVERY print since the spin and never cut: Q2-26 (07-30) beat at $0.88 adj EPS vs $0.77 est on sales $1,148M (+11%) and RAISED FY26 to sales $4,125-4,185M / adj EBITDA $1,035-1,055M / adj EPS $2.75-2.95. Nuclear +27% (sole US UF6 supplier via the ConverDyn JV), Electronic Materials +15%. Ruling: DE-RATE, unambiguously - the estimate path is up and the multiple compressed on deal dilution. THE LIVE SPECIAL-SITUATION VARIABLE: at $62.23 ESI holders receive $10.00 + 0.500x62.23 = $41.12 vs the $50.10 implied at announcement, DOWN 17.9% - the SOLS decline mechanically shrinks the consideration, raising the odds the ESI vote fails or the deal must be sweetened. Path check is favourable: the $53.87 low is ~5 sessions old and SOLS is +15.5% off it - an EARLY bounce. INDEX TRAP (verified two ways, S&P DJI releases + Vanguard ETF holdings): three re-classifications in five months - S&P 500 eff 2025-10-30, DELETED to SmallCap 600 eff 2025-12-22, promoted to MidCap 400 eff 2026-03-23; Russell 1000. Anyone assuming the spinco kept Honeywell's S&P 500 seat had the flow sign backwards twice.
honesty_flag: REVIEW (not ELEVATE) - absence of expected DISCLOSURE. Solstice was contractually allocated 'all environmental liabilities associated with the Solstice Advanced Materials business' and must indemnify Honeywell 'including toxic tort or other hazardous material exposure claims, for UNCAPPED amounts' (10-K Item 1A), against a recorded reserve of only $54M, and states it cannot estimate a range of reasonably possible loss in excess of recorded liabilities. Yet the strings PFAS, polyfluoroalkyl, PFOA and 'forever chemical' appear ZERO times across the FY2025 10-K, the Q2-26 10-Q and the Form 10 information statement - only four hits of generic 'future regulations related to fluorinated chemistries'. For a $9.9B company whose largest segment is fluorine-value-chain refrigerants, and with HFO degradation to TFA an active EU regulatory question, that is a conspicuous omission of a risk TOPIC. Classified REVIEW rather than ELEVATE because it is an omission, not a divergence between a marketed takeaway and disclosed data. Not asserting a liability exists - recording that the most predictable tail in the industry is unaddressed.
